newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SKB says H1 pre-tax profit down.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SKB says H1 pre-tax profit down.

text.p: Slovenia's second largest bank SKB said on Friday its pre-tax profit for the first half of 1997 fell to 1.7 billion tolars ($10.1 million) from 1.8 billion in the same period last year.
"The profit is lower because expenses for bad loans have increased due to worse conditions in the economy and stricter rules imposed by the Bank of Slovenia," Klara Kahrimanovic of SKB told Reuters.
"Another reason for the decline in profit is that the tolar exchange rates lag behind domestic inflation," she added.
She said the bank expected to reach a net profit of 1.85 billion tolars for the whole of 1997, up from 1.79 billion in 1996.
Balance sheet assets are expected to climb to 248.3 billion tolars by the end of 1997 from 208.3 billion tolars at the end of 1996.

In the first six months balance sheet assets rose to 225.7 billion tolars from 192.3 billion mainly due to increased tolar and foreign exchange deposits of individuals and companies. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439 ($ = 167.5 Slovenian Tolars)
